message.content:
Based on my search, here is information about the bones of the head (skull):

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). The skull is divided into two main parts:
- The **neurocranium** (braincase) - protects the brain
- The **viscerocranium** (facial skeleton) - forms the face

## Cranium/Neurocranium (8 bones)

The cranium forms the protective housing for the brain and consists of 8 bones:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and roof of the orbits; contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the foramen magnum for spinal cord passage |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base; house structures of the middle and inner ear |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base; contains sella turcica (houses pituitary gland) |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of nasal cavity |

## Facial Skeleton/Viscerocranium (14 bones)

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | Lower jaw; the only movable bone of the skull |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Upper jaw; form part of orbit and most of hard palate |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Cheekbones |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in medial walls of orbits; house lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form posterior part of hard palate |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Project into nasal cavity; aid airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms inferior portion of nasal septum |

## Key Sutures (Joints)

The bones of the skull are connected by fibrous joints called sutures:
- **Coronal suture**: between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture**: between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture**: between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture**: between parietal and temporal bones

## Additional Bones

The **hyoid bone**, while not part of the skull proper, is often associated with it. It is located in the neck and provides attachment for muscles of the tongue and larynx.

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
